title: NovaSearch — Hosted embeddings + rerank demo
summary: Demo focused on Redwood hosted embeddings API and reranking endpoint for improving search relevance. Discussed integration paths, latency/cost tradeoffs, KV/prefix caching, security (SOC 2, VPC), pilot benchmarks, and next steps (share pricing, run 1-week benchmark, security docs).
topics: Search relevance demo with example queries
Latency vs cost / batching and caching

Priya Nair; Share sample embedding code snippet and quickstart notebook; due 2027-11-12
Maya Patel; Provide 10k query set and current rerank labels for benchmark; due 2027-11-14

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-10 15:00 PST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE briefly), Maya Patel (NovaSearch Head of Search), Tom Ruiz (Eng Manager), Lena Zhou (ML Engineer), Samir Dixit (Security)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. I'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. With me is Priya, our SE, and Marcus might hop in a little bit later. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya: Good thanks. Happy to be here. We wanted to see the hosted approach for embeddings and rerank — we've been evaluating a couple options.
[00:20] Tom: Yep hi all. Our main goal is improving search relevance on product pages, lower latency, keep costs predictable.
[00:28] Alex: Great, that's exactly what we'll walk through. Quick agenda — 1) quick product overview, 2) embeddings API, 3) reranking endpoint and demo with your example queries, 4) integration patterns and security, 5) next steps. Sound good?
[00:35] Maya: Sounds good.
[00:40] Priya: Cool, I'll start with the embeddings piece. So Redwood's hosted embeddings API is a simple REST/SDK call. You post a document or chunk, we return a vector. We also support batch calls and streaming for larger payloads. One note — we have a few tuned models in the catalog, and the runtime will pick optimized kernels depending on sequence length.
[01:05] Tom: Quick Q — do you run the models on dedicated infra or is it multi-tenant?
[01:10] Alex: For hosted it's multi-tenant but we offer Dedicated pools if you want reserved capacity. For the pilot we usually start hosted to move fast and then bump to Dedicated if you need throughput guarantees.
[01:20] Lena: How are you handling caching? We have a lot of near-duplicate content so caching embeddings could help.
[01:26] Priya: Good question. Redwood does automatic prefix/KV caching for inference — it's TTL-based and cache hits avoid recomputation for repeated prefixes. For embeddings specifically you can cache client-side too; we also offer a vector-store integration pattern where embeddings are persisted in your vector DB and we just handle generation.
[01:46] Maya: Any recommendations for dimensionality or model family? We're using 1536 dims today with a third-party embedder.
[01:52] Priya: 1536 is common and maps well to our mid-sized models; if you care about cost we can recommend quantized variants; Redwood Optimize will give model and quantization suggestions per workload. For higher recall jobs you might go 2048, but that's cost right.
[02:10] Tom: Ok. Can you show the rerank endpoint? That's the main interest.
[02:15] Priya: Sure — the reranker is a hosted endpoint that accepts query, top-K candidates (ids + text or embeddings), and returns a reranked list + scores and optional explainability tokens. We'll demo a simple flow: 1) use embeddings API to encode query and docs, 2) search vector DB to get top 50, 3) call rerank with the query and those 50 candidates to refine ordering.
[02:40] [screen share noise]
[02:45] Priya: Alright sharing my screen — here is the console. Top-left you can see a route for "embeddings/generate" and "rerank/score". I'm going to run a very small example dataset — product pages for headphones, some ambiguous queries like "best wireless headphones" where baseline retrieval surfaces popularity but not intent.
[03:10] Maya: Just a heads up, our team cares about latency under 150 ms tail for rerank.
[03:15] Priya: Understood. For the hosted rerank we typically see median around 60-120 ms depending on candidate size and model; tail can be improved with smaller models or dedicating capacity for low jitter. Also batching and continuous KV cache for recurring queries helps.
[03:34] Tom: Do you have benchmarks for rerank vs a traditional BM25 + dot-product retrieval?
[03:40] Priya: We do — I'll share the benchmark spreadsheet post-call. In general, a two-stage retrieval (fast retrieval + rerank) increases relevance (NDCG) significantly with a small latency cost. In our internal tests a small reranker gave +12-18% NDCG on product search scenarios versus dot-product only.
[04:00] Alex: And cost-wise you can pick a smaller rerank model — the rerank stage operates on say 50 candidates so per-query token cost is limited. If you want to optimize cost we can recommend model family and quantization.
[04:15] [05:00] Priya: I'm going to run a live rerank now. Query: "best wireless headphones for running". Baseline retrieval top result is a high-popularity over-ear model; our reranker reorders to favor sweat-resistant in-ear suggestions. Running...
[05:30] [05:40] Priya: Ok response returned — rerank score shows the in-ear model at top now. I'll paste the raw response in chat. You'll notice we include per-candidate relevance score and an optional snippet explaining why it was promoted (keywords matched, intent).
[06:00] Lena: That snippet explanation looks helpful, but how reliable are those explainers for auditing?
[06:05] Priya: They're heuristic; think of them as pointers rather than formal proofs. For audit-quality you can enable structured outputs with deterministic boxes or run unit tests in the eval harness. Redwood Optimize ties evals to prompt sets and can alert on regressions.
[06:25] Samir: From security perspective — do you persist query text on Redwood? How long are logs retained? We need audit logs and data residency.
[06:35] Alex: For hosted we keep logs by default for 30 days; we can support longer retention as an add-on. For full control you can use Private/VPC deployments or Dedicated with egress controls. We also support customer-managed KMS and HSM for keys and provide SOC 2 and ISO artifacts. We'll share the security pack after this call.
[07:00] Tom: Great. Regarding integration — our infra is on AWS, using an existing vector DB (we use Pinecone today). What's the recommended integration pattern?
[07:10] Priya: Many customers keep embeddings in Pinecone/Weaviate and call Redwood for generation. Pattern: 1) batch embed existing corpus and upsert to vector DB, 2) on query, embed the query or use cross-encoder features, 3) retrieve top-K from your DB, 4) call Redwood rerank with the retrieved candidates. We include sample SDKs for Node/Python and a notebook.
[07:35] Maya: If we want to do rerank without sending full doc text (privacy), can we send embeddings only?
[07:42] Priya: Yes. Rerank endpoint accepts embeddings for candidates and the query embedding; we then compute cross-scores. That avoids sending PII text. Note though some explainability features need text, but it's optional.
[08:00] Tom: Latency question — what's the network egress path? If we host in us-west-2 region what's typical RTT?
[08:10] Alex: We have regional endpoints; for us-west-2 you should expect sub-10 ms network RTT from AWS infra within the same region plus model inference time. For tail latency it's best to test with your traffic shape; we can run a benchmark.
[08:30] Priya: I'll switch to a slightly deeper technical slide — a bit of the runtime. We use continuous batching, kernel selection, KV cache for autoregressive workloads, but for rerank it's more of a forward encode/score path so we pick a cross-encoder optimized kernel.
[08:50] [09:10] Maya: You mentioned quantization — can you quantify model size vs performance tradeoff? We don't want regressions in relevance.
[09:18] Priya: Sure. In our tests int8 quantization usually gives ~1-3% quality delta depending on model and task, but 2-4x throughput and huge cost savings. Redwood Optimize will recommend the best quant profile per workload and can run A/B to verify. For initial POC we suggest a small unquantized model to prove quality, then iterate with quantized variants for cost.
[09:45] Tom: Ok sounds reasonable.
[09:50] [10:00] Priya: Let's run a slightly larger scenario — i uploaded a 200 doc product set (demo data) and we'll show end-to-end pipeline: embed -> retrieve -> rerank -> final results. I'm going to artificially inject an ambiguous query that often surfaces non-relevant items, and show the delta.
[10:30] [10:50] Priya: Running retrieval now... got top-50, calling rerank, returning in ~120ms. You can see here the final NDCG improved in the small testset by ~0.15. Again those are demo numbers.
[11:10] Lena: Can we control reranker verbosity? We don't want long explainers in prod.
[11:15] Priya: Yes you can toggle fields in the response and set max tokens for any optional text.
[11:22] Tom: For pricing, do you charge per token + per-embedding unit?
[11:27] Alex: Hosted pricing is usage-based — per-embedding unit and per-token for generation/rerank. Dedicated is negotiated. We'll send a pricing sheet; for pilot we can also offer a credit to run initial benchmark.
[11:40] Maya: Security — can you support SAML/SSO and RBAC?
[11:44] Alex: Yes, SAML SSO for the Console and API keys can be scoped. RBAC roles are supported, logs are available. For Private deployments we add network restrictions and customer-managed KMS.
[11:58] [12:10] Samir: About compliance — do you have SOC 2 Type II? Also need pen test report.
[12:16] Alex: We have SOC 2 Type II and will share the pack. Pen test summary is available; for more we can set an NDA and share redacted reports.
[12:30] Tom: For the pilot benchmark — what's a minimal scope?
[12:35] Priya: Minimal recommended: 10k real queries, embed corpus of your top 200k docs (or subset), run a 1-week live test capturing tail latency, costs, and NDCG against your labels. We can provision keys, run parallel runs, and share dashboards in Redwood Console.
[12:55] Maya: That aligns with our wants. We'll provide a 10k query set and labels.
[13:02] Alex: Great. I'll capture next steps.
[13:06] [13:15] Marcus: (joins) Hey everyone, Marcus from Redwood — quick note on observability: the Console exposes per-route token breakdowns, latency percentiles, and trace hooks. You can also ingest traces into your APM.
[13:30] Maya: Nice.
[13:33] [13:40] Priya: One thing to call out: if you want deterministic low tail latencies you can use Dedicated capacity and pin the rerank model. That reduces cold-start effects and jitter.
[13:52] Tom: What about data residency? Some of our users are EU only.
[13:57] Alex: We have regions in EU and can enforce residency in VPC/private. For full control, Private deployment is an option. For pilot we can run EU region.
[14:10] Maya: Any gotchas around rate limits during the pilot?
[14:15] Priya: We'll set suitable quotas for the pilot and can increase. Also for bursty traffic consider autoscaling policies for Dedicated.
[14:28] [14:40] Tom: One last performance Q — what's your approach to re-ranking long documents? Some product descriptions are 2k tokens.
[14:48] Priya: For long docs we recommend chunking and either merging candidate scores or using a cross-encoder on a condensed summary. The runtime does chunk-aware encoding and we can recommend a strategy based on your distribution.
[15:05] Maya: Ok thanks, this is helpful.
[15:08] Alex: Wrapping up — recap: Redwood will send pricing + pilot proposal, security pack (SOC 2, pen test summary), Priya will share sample code and notebook, customer to provide 10k query set and sample docs. Redwood will provision test keys and run a 1-week benchmark.
[15:30] Maya: Sounds good. Can we get the pilot started next week?
[15:33] Alex: Yes we'll aim to spin up the test keys and schedule a kickoff.
[15:36] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[15:38] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up via email and i'll attach the benchmark sheet.

End of transcript. Some minor transcription issues: speaker labels occasionally overlap and a few technical terms appear as 'K V cache' or 'V P C' in the auto transcript.")
